candidate.title: NSCR
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina NSCR (nascent strand capture and release) schematic for enriching origin-proximal short nascent DNA: genomic replication material → denaturation/size selection → 5′ biotinylation → streptavidin capture → RNase I release → isolation and amplification → DNA. The leftmost NSCR image is a method-identifying icon, followed by the starting replication-bubble illustration. This is one workflow, with a retained-bead branch at RNA cleavage. The depicted endpoint is amplified DNA; the primary paper clarifies its interface to a subsequent sequencing library, without making that unshown preparation another diagram operation.

states.label: Genomic replication material containing RNA-primed nascent DNA
features: The DNA replication bubble is the biological starting illustration, not an isolated-bubble selection step.
Blue parental DNA surrounds a nascent strand whose short magenta segment is labeled RNA primer.
The target SNS is a covalent 5′-RNA–DNA-3′ chimera; its RNA leader must remain intact until selective release.

operations.label: Denaturation and size-selection
operations.description: Heat-denature genomic replication material to release nascent strands, then size-select a short single-stranded fraction. The retained material still mixes RNA-primed SNS with broken genomic DNA.
operations.mechanism: Denaturation followed by sucrose-gradient size fractionation; the cited ~400–2000 nt fraction separates the intended origin-proximal SNS class from shorter Okazaki fragments.
operations.information_effect: Enriches the relevant size class while retaining genomic sequence identity and the RNA leader needed for later selection. Size selection alone does not distinguish SNS from similarly sized broken gDNA.

operations.label: 5′-biotinylation
operations.description: Attach biotin to the 5′ ends of both classes in the size-selected fraction. SNS receives a handle on its RNA-containing end, while broken gDNA also becomes capture competent.
operations.mechanism: The primary implementation uses T4-PNK with ATPγS for 5′ end labeling followed by biotin-maleimide coupling; this is one end-labeling block in the Illumina schematic.
operations.information_effect: Adds the attachment handle used for capture. Labeling does not itself identify a DNA molecule as a replication-origin product.

operations.label: Streptavidin pull-down
operations.description: Bind the 5′-biotinylated fraction to streptavidin beads, converting soluble SNS and gDNA into a bead-associated mixed population.
operations.mechanism: Biotin–streptavidin binding immobilizes labeled fragments. The paper identifies magnetic beads; the schematic shows the support and attached strands.
operations.information_effect: Establishes the physical tether that makes subsequent RNA cleavage a release selection. Both gDNA and SNS are captured at this point.

operations.label: RNase I digestion
operations.description: Treat captured molecules with RNase I. Cleavage in the SNS 5′ RNA leader disconnects its DNA portion from the bead tether, yielding a released DNA fraction and a retained bead-associated fraction.
operations.mechanism: RNase I digests the RNA primer through which the SNS DNA is attached. Primers/remnants and uncleaved gDNA remain bead associated; RNase I is the cleavage reagent, not a transferred product.
operations.information_effect: Selects on an RNA-containing covalent tether rather than on DNA sequence. This enriches nascent DNA but is not perfect biological specificity: incorporated ribonucleotides in other DNA can also permit release in the tested implementation.

operations.label: Isolate and amplify SNS
operations.description: Isolate the released fraction from the retained beads and amplify its DNA. The primary implementation identifies this amplification as WGA; the diagram groups isolation and amplification into one block ending in DNA.
operations.mechanism: Amplification of the RNase I-released SNS fraction; the broad depicted block is retained without adding internal amplification or library-preparation steps.
operations.information_effect: The amplified genomic DNA supplies a downstream sequencing library in which enrichment of origin-proximal sequences supports mapping putative active replication origins. The RNA leader supplied the selection association and is not the intended readout. WGA loses original strand orientation and may bias sequence abundance, so the product does not preserve intact original SNS lengths or provide an unbiased census of initiation events.

method_scopes.rationale: NSCR expands to nascent strand capture and release; these are one method, not separate targets. The card title, diagram label and verified collection-page heading/caption identify a single NSCR workflow. The primary paper’s origin-proximal SNS implementation supports all five local operation instances. Size selection, biotin labeling, capture, RNase I release and amplification are components; no alternative method branch is depicted. The post-cleavage retained beads are a material branch, not another assay.
